headline: Sales and profit both climb; full-year outlook raised
summary_short: Boston Scientific reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.442 billion, up 7.5% y/y, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.61 (+15.1% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $0.86, beating the company's own $0.82-$0.84 guidance range.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.5% y/y ($5.442B; 7.0% organic), topping 5.5%-7.5% guidance, led by Cardiovascular (+8.3%, $3.624B) and MedSurg (+5.9%); U.S. sales grew 6.2%, APAC 11.2%. GAAP diluted EPS of $0.61 rose 15.1% y/y as operating income grew 43.8% on lower restructuring ($8M vs $83M) and no impairment (vs $46M a year ago), partly offset by a new $76M litigation charge; adjusted EPS of $0.86 beat the $0.82-$0.84 guided range. Boston Scientific now guides full-year adjusted EPS to $3.28-$3.32, full-year sales growth to 5.5%-6.5% reported / 5%-6% organic, and Q3 adjusted EPS to $0.80-$0.82. Cash fell to $539M (-62.9% q/q) after a $2B buyback and a $1.5B MiRus LLC investment.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based: Cardiovascular +8.3% reported ($3.624B) and MedSurg +5.9%, with APAC +11.2% and LACA +22.4% regional growth; results topped the company's own 5.5%-7.5% guidance range.

43.8% y/y growth against 7.5% revenue growth reflects lower restructuring charges ($8M vs $83M a year ago) and no intangible impairment (vs $46M a year ago), partly offset by a new $76M litigation-related charge.
Tracks the operating-income improvement described above; net income attributable to shareholders rose to $907M from $797M a year ago.
Decline reflects completing the previously announced $2 billion accelerated share repurchase program and a $1.5 billion equity investment in MiRus LLC during the quarter.
Company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.28-$3.32 and guided Q3 adjusted EPS to $0.80-$0.82, citing confidence in long-term growth anchored by its category-leadership strategy.
